findings.claim: The verifier is told to locate a memorycard topic via mem_search, then mem_get, but its tool list has only mcp__memorycard__mem_get (and Pi's mem_get). It has no mem_search, so it cannot resolve a topic to an id. The old line said 'Engram topic via mem_get_observation'. The new core-prefix line now names a tool the verifier does not have. The same line sits in agents/verifier.md, pi/agents/verifier.md and codex/agents/verifier.toml. The tests only compare the line text and tool lists, so none of them catches this.
evidence: Diff lines 113-118 and 205-217 show verifier tools = 'Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, mcp__memorycard__mem_get' while the body line now says 'via mem_search, then mem_get'.
engine/agentgen/roles.go hasMemoryTool() keeps the shared line for any role with any memorycard tool, so the verifier keeps a line instructing a tool it lacks.
The old text pointed only at mem_get_observation, which the verifier had. The commit added the mem_search reference.

findings.claim: The Pi tool names for memorycard (mcp__memorycard__mem_*) are unverified. gentle-pi drops unknown tool names without a word, so if the real Pi names differ, every role that loses its memory tools on Pi gets no error. The commit's own comment concedes the assumption. The new test TestThePiToolsOfEveryRoleAreNamesTheInstalledSourcesRegister only checks against a hand-edited allowlist of the same assumed names. It pins nothing about what Pi registers, although its comment still claims the names are 'the ones the installed sources register'.
evidence: roles.go comment in the diff: 'This one is an assumption, not verified'.
roles_test.go known map adds the assumed mcp__memorycard__* names, so the test is circular.
The same comment says Pi 'drops a name it does not know without a word', so a wrong name means silent loss of memory access on Pi.
